hook: At Fort Loudoun Dam, 196 failed welds on the discharge ring drove costs to $55.8 million.

sections.voiceover: At Fort Loudoun Dam, 196 failed welds on the discharge ring drove costs to $55.8 million.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a damaged industrial weld on a large metal ring.
sections.sfx_cue: Metallic clinking sound followed by a low hum.

sections.voiceover: The Tennessee Valley Authority began a rebuild of Unit 2 near Lenoir City, Tennessee, to extend its life by 40 years. Why did this project balloon to $55.8 million?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Lenoir City, Tennessee, followed by a wide shot of the dam interior.

sections.voiceover: A November 4 Office of Inspector General report revealed 196 of 240 discharge ring welds failed.
sections.visual_cue: Document graphic highlighting the Office of Inspector General report findings.

sections.voiceover: The Tennessee Valley Authority installed a 375,000-pound turbine to replace the 80-year-old original unit.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing the cost escalation graph.
b_roll: Chart showing 27.4 million vs 55.8 million dollars

sections.voiceover: These failures pushed costs to $55.8 million, far exceeding the original $27.4 million project authorization.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing the final cost figure $55.8 million.
